messages:
maria: quick FYI, ran a short perf sweep on host parsing after the kernel selector tweak. overall host CPU for small-stream requests jumped ~15%. looks concentrated in HTTP/2 frame processing and tokenization allocs.
rahul: do we have a flamegraph or pprof?
maria: uploaded a flame to the gist. highlights from profile: decode_http2_frame heavy, tokenize_chunk hot, kv_cache eviction ticked up. sample:

  31.8%  net/proto  [.] decode_http2_frame
  19.4%  host/token  [.] tokenize_chunk
  11.7%  kvcache    [.] eviction_hotpath

jamie: that smells like more tiny frames hitting the host after we preferred the small-batch kernel. are we copying more or parsing more?
maria: trace lines show many small reads with multiple allocations per frame. example: 

  2026-03-20T14:12:03Z hostA grpc: read 64 bytes -> hpack decode (allocs=14)
  2026-03-20T14:12:03Z hostA tokenize: fragment=32 -> alloc buf -> utf8-normalize

maria: two hypotheses: (1) kernel selector change raises small-batch usage -> higher host pre-parse overhead; (2) kvcache key churn for tiny fragments because we don't canonicalize short prefixes before lookup, leading to eviction storms.
leo: so it's a trade: kernel latency vs host overhead. we'd prefer a change that doesn't push cost to host. could we coalesce small frames before the tokenizer?
rahul: we have an experimental preparse coalescer in the proxy. if we buffer very briefly (few ms) and merge small frames up to a target size, we should reduce syscall and allocation counts without hurting tail latency.
maria: i built a minimal PoC in the Rust proxy: ring buffer that flushes when bytes >= 256 or age >= 6ms. microbench results:

  baseline host CPU per-request: 6.2ms, allocs: 18
  with coalescer: host CPU per-request: 4.1ms, allocs: 4

infra-bot: deploy staging/proxy-coalesce/sha=cb9a2 initiated by maria at 2026-03-20T14:18:12Z
rahul: i'm going to also try a cheap kvcache fix: canonicalize 4-byte prefix before lookup to stabilize keys and avoid micro-evictions. cheap hash + inline path.
jamie: good idea. that plus coalesce should hit both pain points. can you run the perf harness with the kernel selector flag toggled back to the previous small_batch_threshold so we see both directions?
rahul: done. ran 1k mixed-length requests. early numbers:

  p50 latency: baseline 32ms -> canary 30ms
  p95 latency: baseline 120ms -> canary 98ms
  host CPU mean: baseline 6.2ms -> canary 3.9ms
  kvcache eviction rate: baseline 72/min -> canary 9/min

leo: KV drop is dramatic. looks like canonical prefix + coalesce is the right mitigation.
maria: next steps: (1) land kvcache prefix canonicalization PR (jamie/jamie? or jamie owns kvcache?), (2) merge proxy coalescer behind feature flag with metrics (coalesce_hits, coalesced_bytes, flush_age_ms), (3) update kernel selector doc to note host parse tradeoffs and recommended thresholds.
jamie: i'll take the kvcache PR. plan to canary to prod after 24h if no regressions. also will add a small unit test for prefix stability to avoid future regressions.
leo: ops/dash: add panels for tokenization allocs, http2 frame count per request, coalesce hit rate, kvcache eviction rate. add alert if coalesce hit rate <5% for 5m.
maria: i'll write a short runbook/retro in #postmortems after we confirm prod numbers and include the kernel selector decision matrix. thanks all :thumbsup:
